newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cockerill ups job cuts target to 2,135.
newsitem.headline: Cockerill ups job cuts target to 2,135.

text.p: Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre SA said on Wednesday it aims to cut its workforce by 2,135 to 7,777 by the year 2000 as part of its Horizon 2000 plan to curb costs and crank up competitiveness.

Christophe Weerts, spokesman for Belgium's largest steel maker, announced the figures after lengthy talks with unions on Tuesday. Further talks on how the job cuts were to be achieved would begin next week and conclude by the end of June, he told Reuters.
Cockerill booked a 9.00 billion franc loss in 1996, reversing a 3.2 billion franc net profit in 1995, in part because of a 7.7 billion franc exceptional loss.
It set aside six billion francs of provisions to cover part of the costs of the Horizon 2000 plan.
The aim was to trim staff mainly via early retirement. Of Cockerill's current staff of 9,900 over 1,200 are 52 years old or older and as a result qualify for early retirement.
Cockerill had initially set a target of 2,000 job losses in its Horizon 2000 project. It has said the redundancies could be completed by the end of 1998.
The steel maker has said previously it is possible it could make a slight profit in 1997 because of the Horizon 2000 plan.

It expects 1997 steel volumes to be higher than those of 1996 in terms of tonnage, but average steel sales prices to be slightly lower than in 1996, partly because the company is locked into contracts made when prices were less favourable.
